label: Question 6
t: Right to abortion in the state constitution (2nd vote)
what: Adds a fundamental right to abortion until fetal viability, or later when needed to protect the patient's life or health, to the Nevada Constitution; the state may restrict it only for a narrowly defined compelling health interest. Abortion is already legal to 24 weeks under a 1990 voter-approved law. Voters approved this 64.4%-35.6% in 2024; it takes effect only if approved again.
y: The right to abortion before viability is written into the Nevada Constitution.
n: The amendment fails; abortion stays legal to 24 weeks under the 1990 statute.
pro: Nevadans for Reproductive Freedom, Sen. Jacky Rosen (D), Planned Parenthood Votes Nevada, ACLU of Nevada
con: Protect Our Girls, Nevada Right to Life, Americans United for Life, The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints

label: Question 7
what: Requires in-person voters to show photo ID (current or expired up to four years; any age for voters 70+) and mail voters to give the last four digits of their driver's license or Social Security number, or a county-issued number. Nevada now verifies most voters by signature. Voters approved this 73%-27% in 2024; it takes effect only if approved again.
y: Photo ID (in person) and ID numbers (by mail) become constitutional requirements to vote.
n: The amendment fails; current signature-based verification stays.
pro: Repair The Vote, Nevada Voter ID Coalition, Gov. Joe Lombardo (R), President Donald Trump
con: Nevada Voter Freedom Alliance, Battle Born Progress, Silver State Voices
